expectations.text: The reply opens with a recommendation against a fixed quota of low ratings and says why (it labels a fixed share of every team whatever its actual performance), while taking the CEO's underlying concern seriously.
expectations.evidence: Opens: "I would not build it as he described it. A fixed 10% quota with an automatic exit by end of Q3 is the version most likely to fail..." Why: "A quota puts roughly 120 people into the bottom category by definition, and some of them are performing fine"; "A quota measures the manager's arithmetic, not the person's performance." CEO concern: "I can give you a process that delivers what the CEO wants: a visible bottom category, a 60-day plan, and exits." (Passes the opening test, though the recommendation that follows keeps a target range; see assertion 4.)

expectations.text: The reply cites at least one real piece of evidence on forced or stack ranking, or on what drives performance differences between teams, with its source (for example Microsoft dropping stack ranking in 2013, simulation research on forced distribution, or research on managers' effect on teams).
expectations.evidence: No specific evidence with a source. Only "Well-known companies have dropped forced ranking after it reduced collaboration and gamed ratings (Microsoft is the usual example) [M]", with no year or source, and "The skill's reference says manager quality drives most of engagement variance", which cites the assistant's own material rather than a study. A vague nod.

expectations.text: The reply flags that the works council must consent to the appraisal system in both countries (Netherlands: article 27(1)(g) WOR or its consent right on staff appraisal; Germany: §94 BetrVG appraisal principles), and that a plan starting from a ranking is weak ground for a later dismissal (the Dutch court expects timely notice, support and a real chance to improve; in Germany a low-performance dismissal usually needs a warning and proof).
expectations.evidence: NL: "A new appraisal system generally needs the OR's consent under the Works Councils Act"; employer "must show the employee was told what was wrong and given a genuine chance to improve... A quota is not a ground." DE: "The Betriebsrat has co-determination rights over appraisal principles and general evaluation criteria"; performance dismissal "typically requires prior warnings (Abmahnung), a negative prognosis, and a proportionality test. Being in a ranking's bottom band doesn't satisfy that." No article numbers, but the substance is right.

expectations.text: The reply delivers a usable alternative process: clear expectations per role, calibration that aligns standards and checks for bias without forcing a distribution, and individual handling of real underperformance with support and a realistic period.
expectations.evidence: Calibration enforces a distribution: "My recommendation: calibrated ranking with a target range, not a quota"; a full guideline curve (5-10% / 20-25% / 55-65% / 8-12% / 2-5%), and "the ranges are enforced in calibration"; the manager briefing tells managers "We expect... roughly 10-15% across the company to land in the two lowest categories." The plan is a fixed 60 days ("Don't extend plans indefinitely") with no allowance for role complexity. Fails the 'without forcing a distribution' part.

expectations.text: The reply includes a check of ratings by group (such as gender, age, part-time or people on leave) before ratings are used for pay, plans or exits.
expectations.evidence: April calibration: "Bias and adverse-impact check on the output (gender, age, nationality, part-time, leave, disability)", before May rating conversations and plans; "the distribution is checked against... the adverse-impact analysis before anything is final."

expectations.text: The reply gives the user a line or approach for a private conversation with the CEO first, and a usable manager briefing or its outline.
expectations.evidence: 'Your decision' gives a framing for the CEO: "Frame it this way: 'I'm designing it to deliver the outcome and survive a works council and a labour court, not to dilute it.'" plus fallback minimum asks if he insists. A full manager briefing draft is included. (It doesn't explicitly say to raise it privately first, but this is a one-to-one CPO-CEO step before any announcement.)

overall_quality.evidence: The legal gates and manager guidance are useful, but it replaces the quota with a 'target range' enforced in calibration and invokes 'the skill' as its evidence, so it still anchors managers on a share of low ratings and gives the CPO little real evidence to bring to the CEO.

factual_errors.evidence: (1) Labels assumed or self-sourced figures as verified: '[V] The ranges come from the skill's calibrated distribution' and 'spans of 6-10 [V]', though the user gave no span data and the 'healthy 8-12%' benchmark has no real source. (2) Minor imprecision: in the Dutch performance-dismissal bullet, 'Dismissal also requires going through the UWV or the court'. A performance dismissal goes only to the cantonal court.

skill_leak.evidence: "The skill benchmarks I work from", "the skill's calibrated distribution", "the skill's 4-step framework", "The skill is explicit", "the skill's red-flag list", "verified against the people-strategy reference".

owns_result.evidence: The prompt is a proposed policy, not a bad outcome.

best_insight.value: If the CEO insists on a hard quota, the minimum asks: apply it at function level, make the bottom band trigger a diagnosis rather than an exit, and treat end of Q3 as a target, not a promise.

suggestions.assertion: The reply delivers a usable alternative process: clear expectations per role, calibration that aligns standards and checks for bias without forcing a distribution, and individual handling of real underperformance with support and a realistic period.
suggestions.reason: Several samples swap the quota for a company- or function-level 'expected range' (e.g. 10-17% at the bottom) drawn from an unsourced framework. Add a check that no expected or target share is introduced, or that any reference range is sourced and never used to move a rating.

suggestions.assertion: The reply gives the user a line or approach for a private conversation with the CEO first, and a usable manager briefing or its outline.
suggestions.reason: Nearly any CEO talking point passes. Consider requiring that the conversation comes before ExCo, managers or works councils and that it tests what 'it worked at his last company' meant (measure, period, legal setting).

No assertion checks that the reply separates a possible cost or headcount goal from performance management (restructuring route, collective-dismissal rules if exits are driven by a fixed number). The strongest samples do this.
No assertion checks the Dutch route for a performance dismissal (cantonal court, not UWV); at least one sample gets this wrong and still passes assertion 3.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertion 4 correctly fails a design that enforces a target range; assertion 2 correctly fails an unsourced nod to Microsoft.
